parameters.name: deliveredAfter
parameters.description:
Delivery-date range, filtering `Project.deliveryEnabledAt`.

IMPORTANT: `deliveryEnabledAt` is the LATEST delivery — it is overwritten
every time the project is delivered again (revision re-deliveries,
re-sends), so this filter means "most recently delivered in this range",
not "was ever delivered in this range". A project delivered in March and
re-delivered in May does NOT match a March range.

A bare `YYYY-MM-DD` covers the whole UTC day on both ends, so
after = before = one day returns that day's deliveries.

parameters.name: firstDeliveredAfter
parameters.description:
FIRST-delivery range, filtering `Project.firstDeliveredAt` — written once,
the first time the job was delivered, and never overwritten.

This is the counterpart to deliveredAfter/deliveredBefore above, which read
`deliveryEnabledAt` (the LATEST delivery). Both exist because both questions
are real and they give different answers whenever a job is re-delivered:
"what did we deliver in March" wants the first delivery, "what is live /
most recently delivered" wants the latest. A job first delivered in March
and re-delivered in July is in a March range here, and in a July range
there.

Same bare-date semantics as every other range: a `YYYY-MM-DD` covers the
whole UTC day on both ends, so after = before = one day returns that day.

The column is NULL for rows delivered before it existed, so this range only
sees deliveries actually on record — it never infers one from
`deliveryEnabledAt`, which would re-import exactly the ambiguity it exists
to remove.

parameters.name: paymentStatus
parameters.description: Payment status filter: 'paid' → paidAt set; 'unpaid' → paidAt null.

parameters.name: technicianId
parameters.description:
Single technician (saved views + deep links keep sending this). Merged
server-side with `technicianIds`, deduped — the two are one filter.

parameters.name: technicianIds
parameters.description:
Multi-select technicians. Matches a person assigned ANYWHERE on the
project: the legacy `Project.technicianId` scalar, the ProjectTechnician
join, a shoot's own technician, or a shoot's crew.

parameters.name: technicianMatch
parameters.description:
How to combine `technicianIds`:
  - 'any' (default) → the project has at least one of them assigned
  - 'all'           → EVERY selected person is assigned somewhere on the
                      project. Deliberately not "all on the same shoot" —
                      crews are per-visit, and the useful question when
                      auditing a job is who worked it at all.

parameters.name: crewSize
parameters.description:
Shoot-crew size — how many DISTINCT technicians are staffed on the job,
counted across all four places one can be attached (the project scalar,
ProjectTechnician, a LIVE shoot's own technician, and that shoot's crew).

  'solo' | '1'              → exactly one technician
  'crew' | 'team' | 'multi' → two or more
  'N' | 'N+' (N = 1..50)    → N or more
  '' (a cleared select)     → no filter

Unassigned jobs (0 technicians) match NO crew size — that question is
`technicianAssigned=false`.

The pattern deliberately mirrors ProjectsService.parseCrewSizeFilter, which
owns this vocabulary: `whitelist: true` strips anything this DTO does not
declare, so a value the parser understands but this regex rejects would be
unreachable code, while anything this lets through that the parser does not
accept (N outside 1..50) gets a 400 from the parser itself. Keep the two in
step.

NOT applied by buildProjectFilters. Prisma cannot express a to-many
cardinality in `where` (no `_count`, no self-correlation), so this resolves
through a pre-query that is AND-ed onto the clause — and it has to happen on
the list, the ids ("select all") AND the metrics query, or the chip count
disagrees with the rows beneath it. ProjectsService.applyCrewSizeFilter is
the one place that does it, and every project-list surface routes through
it.

parameters.name: serviceAreaIds
parameters.description:
Service-area coverage, matched against the DERIVED
`Project.resolvedServiceAreaId` (where the property falls TODAY, re-derived
from lat/lng against the org's current areas) plus two sentinels for the
states that have no id:
  - '__outside__' → placed, and inside no area
  - '__unknown__' → could not be placed at all (no usable coordinates)
They are not uuids, so they cannot collide with a real area id. See
SERVICE_AREA_OUTSIDE / SERVICE_AREA_UNKNOWN in common/utils/filter-builder.

This filter existed as a correct predicate for a while but was withheld
from the DTO, because it pointed at the frozen `Project.serviceAreaId` —
a booking-time BILLING snapshot that InvoicesService reads to choose
per-area pricing, and that carries a value on ~no rows (0 of 3218 on dev).
Filtering it matched nothing, and backfilling it would have changed what
un-invoiced jobs cost. The derived column exists so filtering can be right
without money moving; the frozen column stays frozen.

'__unknown__' is always trustworthy. '__outside__' is not: NULL covers both
"placed, matched nothing" and "nothing was derived", so it needs the
backfill to have run AND the org to have active coordinate-based coverage
(an org with name-based areas only resolves nothing, and every project would
read as outside). See the predicate comment in buildProjectFilters.

parameters.name: travelFeeZoneIds
parameters.description:
Travel-fee zone, matched against the DERIVED
`Project.resolvedTravelFeeZoneId`. Zones are the concentric distance bands
configured inside each service area (they live only in the
`Organization.serviceArea` JSON — there is no zone table), so a zone id is
only meaningful next to its area; pair this with `serviceAreaIds`.

Withheld until now for the same reason as serviceAreaIds: the
`Project.travelFee*` columns are the immutable billing snapshot, frozen so
that moving a zone boundary can never rewrite a historical invoice, and 0%
populated. "Which zone is this property in today" is a different question,
and it gets its own derived column.

parameters.name: pipelineStageId
parameters.description: Kanban stage membership filter (see ProjectFilterParams.pipelineStageId).

parameters.name: importSource
parameters.description:
Filter by import provenance (Project.importSource) — e.g. 'aryeo' to select
only Aryeo-imported projects. Lets "select all across pages" resolve the
Aryeo-only subset server-side (the loaded page can't be filtered for the
off-page rows client-side, since importSource only rides on loaded cards).

parameters.name: schedulingStatus
parameters.description:
Partition the list by scheduling state:
  - 'pending'   → only projects with no shoot time yet (scheduledTime null)
  - 'scheduled' → only projects that have a shoot time (scheduledTime set)
Omitted → both are returned (legacy behaviour). The company Projects
page splits into a "scheduling pending" carousel ('pending') and the
main paginated grid ('scheduled') so the grid's page count reflects
scheduled projects only.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description:
Response shape. `card` returns a LEAN per-project payload with only the
relations a list/board card renders (dropping the deep joins the detail
view uses), which massively cuts the query + JSON for card grids like the
kanban board. Omitted/`full` keeps the historic fat include. Consumers that
pass `card` must hydrate full detail separately (e.g. on opening a job).

parameters.name: addOnIds
parameters.description:
Add-ons selected at booking (`Project.selectedAddOnIds`). Any-of: a
project matches when it carries at least one of the selected add-ons.

parameters.name: includeArchived
parameters.description:
When true, archived projects are included in the result. Defaults to
false (archived projects are hidden). Only the deep "Archived Orders"
settings page should pass true.

parameters.name: archivedOnly
parameters.description:
When true, returns ONLY archived orders — the projects-page "Archived"
filter. Distinct from includeArchived (which returns both). Also opts out
of the default cancelled-exclusion since archived orders are cancelled.

parameters.name: workspaceOrgId
parameters.description:
For AGENT users only: when set, scopes the cross-org "my projects"
list to a specific workspace.
- If the org is COMPANY/TEAM: returns only projects fulfilled by that org.
- If the org is the agent's PERSONAL org: returns only projects fulfilled
  by solo providers (PERSONAL orgs).
- Otherwise: ignored.

parameters.name: deliveredAfter
parameters.description:

every time the project is delivered again (revision re-deliveries,

and re-delivered in July is in a March range here, and in a July range
there.

whole UTC day on both ends, so after = before = one day returns that day.

sees deliveries actually on record — it never infers one from
`deliveryEnabledAt`, which would re-import exactly the ambiguity it exists
to remove.

x-api-key.name: x-api-key
x-api-key.description: Organization API key. The organization is derived from the key, so x-org-id is not required and is ignored if sent. Scoped: READ covers safe methods, WRITE implies READ, ADMIN covers everything, BULK_IMPORT and WEBHOOKS are narrow.

allDay.description: Defaults to true (whole-day). false = a single half day with a time window.

shootsInWindow.description: Shoots already scheduled inside the leave window that need reassigning.

deliverablesDue.description: Deliverables due inside the window and who's covering them.

coverageConfirmed.description:
Requester attests coverage is arranged. When false the request may be
submitted but is NOT self-approvable — it routes to NEEDS_INFO on review.

clientThreads.description: Open client threads that need a hand-off.

pmActionItems.description: Action items the covering PM must own.

policyAcknowledged.description: Requester ticked the time-off policy acknowledgment → stamps a timestamp.

accountType.description:
User-facing intent for the account.
Only AGENT and PROVIDER are user-facing in the UI.

whitelabelOrgId.description:
When the user signs up on a whitelabel custom domain, this is the
orgId of that company. The backend creates an OrganizationCustomer
record so the user lands in that company's customer portal.
When signing up from a whitelabel workspace URL, auto-associate with this org

orgId.description: Optional org ID for whitelabel branding on the OTP email

purpose.description:
Purpose the code is issued for. Scopes how it can later be redeemed:
'signup' (default) rejects already-registered emails; 'login_2fa',
'password_reset' and 'returning_customer_setup' allow them. A code minted
for one purpose cannot be redeemed by another flow.

bonusSpendCents.description:
GRANTED PROGRESS, in cents, as a delta against earned lifetime spend.
Positive grants, negative corrects, 0 removes. Deliberately NOT `@Min(0)`:
a negative grant is how an operator walks back progress handed out in
error. The effective figure is floored at zero where it is read.

tierOverrideSlug.description:
GRANTED TIER pin. Must be an ENABLED tier slug for this org — the service
checks that against LoyaltyTierConfig, because class-validator cannot know
one org's tier list. `null` removes the pin.

reason.description:
Required, and load-bearing rather than decorative: this changes the rate
the customer earns cashback at on every future order, and loyalty credit is
redeemable against an invoice. The service trims and re-checks it, because
a single space passes `@IsString()`.

customerId.description:
An existing OrganizationCustomer in the caller's org. The service re-binds
it to `orgId` before touching anything — a bare id would otherwise let one
org mint a loyalty account against another org's customer.

email.description:
Grant to an email address instead. A recipient with no account is a
FIRST-CLASS case, not an edge case: the service creates (or adopts) the
customer row, mints a pending CUSTOMER invitation so the notification email
has a real signup link, and the reward is waiting when they arrive.

customerName.description:
Display name for a brand-new customer row created by the email arm. Ignored
when the address already belongs to a customer — an existing person's name
is theirs, and a grant is not the place to rename them.

cents.description: discount_next_order_cents — flat cents off the next order.

addOnId.description: free_add_on — PackageAddOn.id. The service checks it belongs to this org.

packageId.description:
free_package — ServicePackage.id.

A free_package reward is 100% off THE MATCHING PACKAGE'S LINE in an order.
It is not, and must never become, a blanket free order: if the customer's
order does not contain this package, the reward is simply not applicable
and the checkout says so. That is why the id is required rather than
optional — an entitlement with no packageId cannot be matched to a line,
and "matches nothing" would have to be resolved either by refusing every
order or by discounting all of them.

config.description: perk_template — the template's own config blob, shape defined per template.

expiresAt.description:
Absolute expiry instant, ISO-8601. OPTIONAL — omitting both this and
`expiresAfterDays` means the reward never expires, which is a supported
outcome rather than a missing value.

expiresAfterDays.description: TTL in days from the moment of the grant. Mutually exclusive with `expiresAt`.

note.description:
Why this was granted. Not required — unlike a manual credit adjustment,
which moves money against a balance — but it is what the audit line reads
six months later, so the UI should ask for it.

displayName.description:
Override the auto-generated label ("Free Premium Package"). The default is
computed from the catalog at grant time and frozen onto the row, so a
renamed package never blanks a customer's pending reward.

category.description:
Raw backend category for this notification's type. Lets clients group /
 filter the inbox without re-deriving the taxonomy from the type.

assignedProjects.description: Preview of the projects in the batch (capped server-side, newest first).

senderName.description:
Display name of the user who sent the message — used by the
 inbox row to surface "From <senderName>" instead of a generic
 "New message" headline.

mentioned.description:
True when THIS recipient was @mentioned in the message body. Lets clients
 render "<senderName> mentioned you" and keep the row out of the
 "N new messages" per-project rollup — an unmissable direct callout rather
 than one more line in the chat firehose.

messageId.description:
The chat message this notification is about. Needed to deep-link to the
 specific message (scroll/highlight), not just the project's chat tab.

cartId.description:
For BOOKING_ABANDONED — the `PendingOrder.id` of the unfinished cart.

Flattened out of the payload rather than left in it for the same reason
`assignedCount` is: a client that reads only `projectId` renders this row
with a dead "View Project" button, because a PendingOrder has no Project by
construction. This id is the `?resume=` target the booking flow, the resume
screen and the checkout-cancel page already use — clients deep-link to
`/booking?resume=<cartId>` and must not invent a second address for it.

videoScriptSetId.description:
For VIDEO_SCRIPTS_READY — the `VideoScriptSet.id` this row announces.

`projectId` is present on this row too (the scripts belong to a listing),
so unlike `cartId` this is not what rescues the row from being untappable.
It is what makes the tap land on the RIGHT thing: a listing accumulates a
set per regeneration, and an agent who asked for a rewrite and then opened
a week-old notification must get the set that notification was about, not
whatever is newest. Flattened out of the payload for the same reason every
field above is — clients read the DTO, not the raw payload blob.

token.description: The push token. For platform=expo this is an ExponentPushToken[…] string. For platform=apns this is the hex-encoded APNs device token from application(_:didRegisterForRemoteNotificationsWithDeviceToken:).

platform.description: Token format. 'expo' = Expo push service (RN app). 'apns' = direct APNs (SwiftUI app, see PRD §6.5). 'ios' / 'android' are accepted for backwards compatibility and treated as expo-format tokens.

bundleId.description: iOS CFBundleIdentifier (e.g. 'com.vremly.agent' or 'com.vremly.virtualxposure'). Required for platform=apns so the multi-tenant APNs sender picks the right auth key + team. Expo tokens omit it.

environment.description: APNs environment the device token was issued by: 'sandbox' for Debug-signed builds (aps-environment=development) or 'production' for App-Store / TestFlight builds. Apple's production gateway returns 200 OK for sandbox tokens but the push silently drops, so the dispatcher must send to the gateway that matches the token. Optional — when omitted the dispatcher falls back to its dual-gateway retry. Send "sandbox" from Swift Debug builds via `#if DEBUG`.

endpoint.description: The push service's delivery URL for this browser. THE identity of the subscription — the row is upserted on it. Must be https and must not resolve to an internal host (see isAcceptablePushEndpoint).

userAgent.description: Browser UA at registration. Display only; never routed on.

origin.description: The origin the service worker was registered from, e.g. "https://app.vremly.com" or a tenant's own domain. Required — a subscription with an unknown origin cannot be attributed to a tenant.

endpoint.description: The endpoint to stop sending to.

shareOrdersWithTeam.description:
AGENT TEAM — "share my orders with my team", DEFAULT true (see
`User.shareOrdersWithTeam` in schema.prisma for the full semantics).

Self-only, exactly like the birthday fields above and for the same reason:
this DTO backs PATCH /users/me and the admin-facing UpdateUserDto
deliberately does NOT carry it, so an org owner cannot flip a colleague's
or a customer's sharing preference for them.

MUST be declared here. main.ts runs class-validator with `whitelist: true`,
so an undeclared key is silently stripped and the toggle would appear to
save and then read back unchanged, with no error anywhere.

birthdayMonth.description:
OPTIONAL birthday — month + day, with the year optional on top. Only ever
settable by the person themselves: this DTO backs PATCH /users/me, and the
admin-facing UpdateUserDto deliberately does NOT carry these fields, so an
org owner cannot write a colleague's or customer's birthday.

Send all three as `null` to clear it.

NOTE the decorator asymmetry, which is intentional:
 - `birthdayMonth` carries the cross-field @Validate and NO @IsOptional, so
   the whole-triple rule runs on every request — including one that sends
   only a day, or only a year, both of which must be rejected.
 - `birthdayDay` / `birthdayYear` carry @IsOptional @IsInt purely so a
   non-numeric value is reported as such; their real validation (range,
   month length, leap year) happens in the constraint above.

emailNotifications.description:
Master email kill-switch. When false, EmailService.shouldSendEmail
suppresses every per-user-gated email category except the legally/
financially exempt ones (see EMAIL_MASTER_EXEMPT_KEYS). This is the
field the "Email Notifications" UI toggle binds to.

emailPropertyAnalytics.description:
Weekly per-listing performance report. Needed here as well as on the model:
ValidationPipe runs `forbidNonWhitelisted`, so a field absent from this DTO
is a 400, not a silent drop — the settings page could not turn this off at
all without it.

allDayFree.description: All-day entries the calendar publishes as FREE (public holidays).

allDayBusy.description: All-day entries the calendar publishes as BUSY (vacation / out-of-office).

tentative.description:
ALL-DAY entries the calendar publishes as TENTATIVE. A TIMED tentative
 entry always blocks and is deliberately not configurable — see
 classifyExternalEvent, whose all-day gate runs first.

sourceProjectId.description: The job the files are copied FROM. Must be a different job, same org.

mediaIds.description:
Media ids on the source job. Re-validated server-side against that project
and against the importable-kind filter — this list is a request, not a
grant.

rawFolder.description:
Optional label grouping these under a folder in the Raw / Source bucket,
matching the folder the operator was browsing. Cosmetic grouping only — the
same field a technician's folder upload already sets.

estimatedDuration.description:
Total shoot length in minutes for the initial appointment, as computed by
the create form (package + add-ons + any manually-added extra time).

ADVISORY, NEVER AUTHORITATIVE. The server resolves the package + add-ons
itself and that is the contract; this number is honoured only when it
EXCEEDS that resolved length — the form's "Add extra time" control is
strictly additive and is the only thing that produces such a number — and is
then recorded as an explicit MANUAL override attributed to the caller. An
equal or SHORTER number never overrules the package: no client can express a
deliberate shortening at booking, so a short number is a stale one.

When the catalogue carries no duration at all, this number is honoured ONLY
if the caller also sets {@link estimatedDurationIsManual}. Otherwise it is
ignored and the shoot is left with no contracted length, which keeps the
payroll flag alive. See `shoot-duration.util.decideBookingDuration`.

estimatedDurationIsManual.description:
"A human typed `estimatedDuration` into an otherwise-empty field."

The ONLY thing that lets a client-supplied number establish a length when
the catalogue is silent. It exists because the number alone cannot carry its
own provenance: every client used to send a FABRICATED value here — the
staff form pre-filled 120 and snapped back to 120 when cleared, the agent
flow held a `useState(120)` nothing ever updated — and the backend recorded
those as `contractedDurationSource = BOOKING`, i.e. "the customer bought two
hours", which then silenced the payroll flag for a shoot whose length nobody
had established.

A number sent WITHOUT this flag is treated as possibly-defaulted and is
dropped when nothing else establishes a length, so an old or cached client
degrades to a flagged shoot rather than to an invented contract. Honoured
values are stamped MANUAL, never BOOKING.

WHO SENDS IT: `JobRequestForm` → `JobManagementContext.createJob` →
`api.projects.create`, and only on the branch where the selected services
carry NO duration of their own — the branch that renders the free-text
"minutes" input. Whatever sits in that input got there by a human act (typed
in, or dragged as a span on the calendar and carried in through
`initialValues`); nothing seeds it, and clearing it leaves it empty. When the
catalogue does answer, the field is read-only and the flag is NOT sent: the
PM's +15m / +30m / +60m top-up is already covered by the longer-than-
catalogue rule, which records the same MANUAL stamp.

selectedAddOnIds.description:
Add-on ids selected in the manual "New Project" flow. Persisted by
projects.service.create (which must read dto.selectedAddOnIds) so the
add-on picks drive the initial invoice — mirroring the update() path that
already accepts this field. Mirrors CreatePublicOrderDto.addOnIds.

bookingAnswers.description:
Booking-question answers collected in the staff "New Project" flow, matching
the questions a customer answers during self-booking. Persisted structured
on Project.bookingAnswers (NOT concatenated into notes) so the "Booking
details" section renders them — mirrors CreateOrderDto/CreatePublicOrderDto.

discountId.description:
THE PROMOTIONAL INCENTIVE A COORDINATOR ATTACHES WHILE BOOKING BY HAND.

`JobRequestForm` → `JobManagementContext.createJob` → `api.projects.create`
is the ONLY client, and this is the door the staff "New Project" dialog
actually goes through (not `POST /orders/create`).

An `OrgDiscount` by row id (a named markdown the org configured) or by
coupon `code` — send EXACTLY ONE. Both, or neither, is refused as
`ambiguous_request` and the project is still created.

── NO AMOUNT CROSSES THE WIRE ─────────────────────────────────────────────
Deliberately. The server re-reads the row in THIS org, re-prices it against
the invoice it actually built and clamps it (`priceCoupon`). A client that
could state its own reduction could make any job free.

── DECLARING THEM IS NOT AUTHORIZING THEM ─────────────────────────────────
`BookingIncentivesService.assertMayApplyIncentives` checks
`invoices.discount:write` IN THE ORG BEING BILLED before any of this is
honoured, because a linked agent-customer arrives as PERSONAL_OWNER of
their own org and passes every naive role check. They are declared here
because `ValidationPipe` runs `forbidNonWhitelisted: true` — an undeclared
field is a 400 and therefore NO PROJECT AT ALL, which would turn a coupon
typo into a lost booking.

rewardEntitlementId.description:
A `LoyaltyEntitlement` THE CUSTOMER ALREADY HOLDS, spent on this job.

A reward is not a coupon and is never applied as one: it is a single-use
asset the customer owns, it reduces the TAXABLE BASE (CRA taxes the
discounted price), and it is claimed with a guarded UPDATE before any

contractedDurationMinutes.description:
The shoot's contracted length in minutes. When set, `endTime` is DERIVED
from it (start + duration) so the calendar block and the pay run can never
describe this shoot differently — the two used to be written by separate
code paths, and `contractedDurationMinutes` was never written at all.

Preferred over `endTime` on this route: the webapp's shoot form leaves the
end-time input optional, so extra shoots were routinely created with
neither an end time nor a length.

MUST stay declared: `whitelist: true` silently strips undeclared fields.

The added shoot's contracted length in minutes. When set, `endTime` is
DERIVED from it so the calendar block and the pay run agree by construction.

When neither this nor `endTime` is sent, an `add_items` shoot falls back to
the total duration of the add-ons it is being CHARGED for
(`pricing.addOnIds`) — the length that was actually sold. A `split` shoot
reuses the order's already-purchased items, so nothing implies a length for
it and it is left with none rather than one being invented.

MUST stay declared: `whitelist: true` silently strips undeclared fields.

THE MANUAL DURATION OVERRIDE, in minutes.

A shoot's length is fixed at booking from the package it was sold with (plus
its add-ons) and may thereafter change ONLY through an explicit gesture like
this one. Sending it rewrites `ProjectVisit.contractedDurationMinutes`, marks
the provenance MANUAL, records who changed it, and derives `endTime` from it
so the calendar block and the pay run cannot describe the same shoot
differently.

WHY IT DID NOT EXIST BEFORE: `contractedDurationMinutes` shipped with a doc
comment promising "a reviewer sets it from the pay run", but no DTO carried
it and no route wrote it — the column had ZERO writers in the entire
product. The nearest thing was the optional end-time input, which rewrote a
span with no record that a human had decided anything. Note that
`payrollOnSiteSecondsOverride` is NOT this field: that corrects the MEASURED
on-site time, this one sets the CONTRACT.

`null` clears it back to "not established", which returns the shoot to being
FLAGGED at pay time rather than paying a number nobody stands behind.

THAT SENTENCE IS TRUE ONLY BECAUSE THE WINDOW IS REMOVED WITH THE STAMP.
`endTime` is DERIVED from this field on every write, so it took two rounds
to make the promise real, and the second round is the one worth knowing:

  • Clearing the stamp ALONE left the derived window in place, and
    `resolveShootPaidSeconds` just dropped from precedence 2 to precedence 3
    and re-paid the identical seconds as a `BOOKED_WINDOW` with an empty
    attention array — the operator withdrew the number and nothing
    downstream heard.
  • Clearing it and REPLACING the window with a placeholder-length one was
    worse on a 60-minute package: `packageCorroboratesVisitSpan` vouches for
    a window that equals the package's own duration, which turns off the
    very refusal the placeholder length was chosen to trigger, so
    withdrawing a 45-minute stamp on such an order RAISED the shoot from
    2700 s to 3600 s, still unflagged.

`resolveVisitTimeWrite` now sets `endTime` to NULL when the window was the
cleared stamp's own derivative. The shoot then states no length at all —
nothing at any precedence, and no window for the package to vouch for — so
it is `SHOOT_DURATION_MISSING` for every package duration, which is the
promise above.

Send `endTime` in the SAME request to mean "clear the number but KEEP this
window" — an explicit window is the caller's own statement and is honoured
as-is (still unstamped). That is what the shoot-duration dialog sends when
it can land on the order's package.

Bounded to a day — a longer shoot is a data-entry slip, and an unbounded
value here would be paid.

which is what the name implied), silently hiding real availability from
customers; and it turned an out-of-hours manual assignment into a hard 409.
The backing column is dropped in the accompanying migration.

`forbidNonWhitelisted: true`, so an unknown key 400s the WHOLE request. A
browser tab opened before this shipped still PUTs `autoDeclineBookings`;
removing the field would break saving availability for those sessions.
Safe to delete once stale clients have rolled over.

visitId.description:
The specific shoot (ProjectVisit) this ping belongs to. Optional for
backward compatibility with clients that predate per-shoot tracking
(Phase 1 crew-reliability), and unavoidable for the 98-of-116 production
projects that have no `ProjectVisit` row at all. Omitting it keeps the
legacy project-level behaviour (keyed on `visitId IS NULL`).

It NO LONGER skips the gates. It used to skip both the assigned-technician
check and the shoot-window check outright, because both lived inside an
`if (visit && …)`. The assigned-technician check now runs on this path too,
against the PROJECT's assignment, and the window check degrades to the
shoot's own local day (a project-level trip has no place in the day's shoot
sequence to be gated against). Passing a visitId still gets the full
per-shoot window, which additionally waits out the technician's previous
same-day shoot.

horizontalAccuracy.description:
`CLLocation.horizontalAccuracy` for THIS ping, in metres — the radius of
the 68%-confidence circle around `latitude`/`longitude`.

WHY IT MUST BE DECLARED HERE: the global pipe runs with
`whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true` (main.ts), so an undeclared
key does not merely get dropped — it 400s the WHOLE ping, and every client
in the tree treats a non-2xx trip POST as a retryable failure. Shipping the
field client-side without this declaration would take the technician's
entire trip offline, not degrade one column.

DELIBERATELY UNBOUNDED. CoreLocation reports a NEGATIVE accuracy when the
fix is invalid, and a cell-tower-only fix legitimately reports thousands of
metres. A `@Min(0)`/`@Max(n)` here would turn "my GPS is poor" into "your
trip failed", so the value is accepted as sent and normalised server-side
(negative / non-finite ⇒ stored as null, i.e. "quality unknown").

Persisted to `ProjectTracking.horizontalAccuracyMeters` on every ping, and
to `ProjectTracking.startAccuracyMeters` for the ping that supplies the
trip ORIGIN — payroll bills kilometres against that origin and has to be
able to reject a 3 km cell-tower fix before it does.

`COMPLETE` on a row that already has a device-recorded completion (that
timestamp is reused verbatim).
