isEnterprise.description: True when the org holds the ENTERPRISE (or FOUNDER) plan AND is paying. This is the PLAN question, not a feature question: an active add-on SKU grants a feature to an org that reads false here, so clients must gate on features[key].granted, never on this.

subscriptionActive.description: Enterprise AND actually paying (active / trialing / past_due, a card-less granted trial, or FOUNDER). False for a lapsed enterprise, which keeps every feature but falls back to the per-transaction fee.

transactionFeePct.description: The percentage a charge would actually take right now: 0 when exempt, otherwise the effective rate including any per-org override. Measured through computePlatformFeeCents, so it cannot disagree with what Stripe takes. Always a number on the wire; null is reserved for clients modelling "not loaded yet".

features.description: One { granted, limit? } per gated feature — the union of the plan grants and any active add-on SKU subscriptions. Clients gate the UI on these so a Free org is shown an upgrade path instead of a button that 403s. Gate on `granted`, never on which SKU was sold: SKUs are repriced and rebundled, entitlement keys are not.

slug.description:
═══ THIS FIELD IS A DNS LABEL, NOT A DISPLAY STRING ══════════════════════

It becomes `<slug>.vremly.com`, which `registerSubdomain` /
`removeSubdomain` interpolate into a Vercel management-API URL PATH. As a
bare `@IsString()` it accepted `../../../../v9/projects/<projectId>#`,
which a URL parser resolves to `/v9/projects/<projectId>` — on the DELETE,
that is "delete the entire Vercel project", carrying VERCEL_API_TOKEN, and
it takes vremly.com and app.vremly.com down together. Reachable by any
authenticated user: create a COMPANY org (you become OWNER), PATCH the slug
to arm it, PATCH again so `slugChanged` fires the teardown.

`@Matches` is the SOURCE half of that fix. `assertProvisionableHost` at
every outbound Vercel URL is the sink half, and neither assumes the other
ran. Reserved-name screening is applied in the service, against the SAME
exported list `generateUniqueSlug` uses on create — see org-slug.ts.

`@MaxLength` is redundant against the pattern and kept anyway: a length
violation reports as a length violation, which is what the person renaming
their company actually needs to be told.

sessionRecordingEnabled.description:
The org's own switch for third-party session recording (Microsoft
Clarity). False stops the recorder for this organisation's staff AND its
portal customers, everywhere, without a deploy — see
Organization.sessionRecordingEnabled in schema.prisma and the fourth gate
in components/shared/analytics/ClarityInit.tsx.

Sits next to the legal links deliberately: the person editing an
organisation's terms and privacy URLs is the person who needs to find it.

videoScriptDefaultLengthSeconds.description:
═══ THE COMPANY'S HOUSE STYLE FOR AI VIDEO SCRIPTS ══════════════════════

The five script controls, set ONCE for the company instead of re-picked on
every generation: length, tone, pace, what the hook leads with, and how far
the writing may depart from a literal description. A per-generation request
overrides any of them individually — the resolution order is REQUEST →
THESE → the built-in, PER FIELD, in `resolveScriptControls`.

THIS IS THE ONLY WRITE PATH THEY HAVE, and it is the reason they are here
rather than only on the generate request. The ORDER-TRIGGERED generation
has no user to ask — it fires from an order-creation hook or a sweep tick —
so it resolves against these columns and nothing else. Without a route a
company that shoots luxury listings could set its house style only through
a psql session, which is how `allowCustomerWebsiteEdits` above spent months
pinned to its default.

`@IsIn` AGAINST THE SHARED ALLOWLISTS, imported rather than restated. These
values are INTERPOLATED INTO AN LLM SYSTEM PROMPT, so the set of legal
strings has exactly one definition (`video-script-controls.ts`) and a
second copy here is how a value this route accepts stops being a value the
prompt understands. Out of range is a 400, never a coercion — and
`resolveScriptControls` checks these columns AGAIN when it reads them, so a
value written by a restored backup still cannot reach the model.

NULL IS MEANINGFUL AND STAYS REACHABLE: it means "this company never chose
one", which is a different fact from "chose the same thing the built-in
says" and stays different if a built-in is ever changed. `@ValidateIf`
admits an explicit `null` so a company can clear a choice; `@IsOptional`
alone would make `null` a validation error and leave no way back.

videoScriptDefaultBoldness.description:
safe | balanced | bold. IT IS NOT A TEMPERATURE SETTING and must never be
made into one — see the docblock on `SCRIPT_BOLDNESS`. It changes the
instruction language the model is given; grounding is absolute at every
value, including `bold`.

allowCustomerWebsiteEdits.description:
"May the listing agent edit their own delivered property website?"

ADDED 2026-08-13. The column has existed and been ENFORCED since the
customer-website-editing work (`listings.service.ts` refuses the edit when
it is false), but it was in no DTO and on no route — the only way to switch
it off was a psql session, and every org therefore ran on the `true`
default. Locking it down per listing
(`ListingWebsiteConfig.customerEditsLockedAt`) was the only reachable
substitute, one listing at a time.

Deliberately NOT given a new default here: the column stays
`@default(true)`, so declaring it changes nothing until somebody flips it.

paymentRoutingMode.description:
HOW this org's customer payments move. OPERATIONAL ONLY.

It does NOT and MUST NOT decide whether the platform charges its fee.
That is `computePlatformFeeCents` (common/plans.ts), which reads the org's
plan and exemptions — never a preference the org sets about itself. Until
2026-08-29 `DIRECT_STRIPE` dropped `application_fee_amount` in all three
charge paths, so this one field was a self-serve waiver of the 3%: the org
kept `transfer_data.destination` (100% of the money) and paid nothing.

`DIRECT_STRIPE` additionally requires staff to have provisioned real
direct settlement (`stripeDirectCharges` / `stripeStandaloneMode`, neither
of which is in this DTO); the service 403s otherwise.

captureStrategy.description:
WHEN THE CUSTOMER'S CARD IS CHARGED at booking checkout.

  IMMEDIATE    — charge at checkout.
  MANUAL_LATER — authorize at checkout; someone captures on delivery via
                 `POST /orders/:projectId/capture`. THE DEFAULT, and the
                 behaviour every checkout had hardcoded before this setting
                 existed. A card authorization lapses after roughly 7 days
                 and nothing captures automatically, so an org on this
                 setting has a real obligation: capture, or lose the sale.

`paymentRoutingMode: ESCROW_LIKE` forces manual capture regardless of what
is sent here — that routing mode *is* "hold the money until the work
lands". Setting IMMEDIATE alongside it is accepted and has no effect; the
UI should say so rather than pretend the pair is contradictory.

autoSendInvoiceOnOrder.description:
Bill at booking. True (the default, and what the platform used to
hardcode) emails the customer their auto-created invoice the moment an
order is placed. False still creates the invoice — it just stays a DRAFT
until staff send it or the project is delivered.

serviceAreaIds.description: Service area IDs this plan is available in (empty = all areas)

priceByAreaCents.description: Per-service-area premium overrides in cents, keyed by service-area id ({ [serviceAreaId]: cents }). Areas not listed fall back to `price`.

coverageWindowHours.description: Coverage window in hours. null = covers any cancellation made before the shoot starts (no hour limit); N = covers cancellations made within N hours of the scheduled shoot.

coversOnSite.description: When true, also covers cancellations after the tech is on-site / after the scheduled start time.

serviceAreaIds.description: Service area IDs this plan is available in (empty = all areas)

priceByAreaCents.description: Per-service-area premium overrides in cents, keyed by service-area id.

coverageWindowHours.description: Coverage window in hours. null = covers any pre-shoot cancellation; N = within N hours of the shoot.

coversOnSite.description: When true, also covers cancellations after the tech is on-site.

autoDeclineBookings.description:
REMOVED FEATURE — accepted and ignored. See AvailabilityStatusDto for the
full reasoning; kept only so a stale client's request is not rejected
wholesale by `forbidNonWhitelisted: true`.

serviceAreaIds.description: Service-area ids from Organization.serviceArea. Empty = derive from the member's home base.

editorMediaTypes.description: Media types this member is auto-routed. Empty = not auto-routable (they can still be assigned by hand, and can still complete anything).

mode.description: ALL = attach every editor who lists this type. SPLIT = attach the least-loaded one.

slaHours.description: Per-media-type production budget in hours. Null clears it and falls back to the org editing budget.

enabled.description: Master switch. Off (the default for every org) means nothing is auto-assigned.

calendarColor.description: Hex colour for this member's calendar events (e.g. "#0369a1"), or null to fall back to the auto-assigned palette colour.

payrollMileageRateCents.description:
Per-member mileage reimbursement, in cents per distance unit — `null` clears
the override so the member falls back to the org default.

`OrganizationMember.payrollMileageRateCents` is READ on every compute
(`member ?? org ?? 0`) and effective-dated into `MemberPayRateVersion`, but
it had no API at all: it was absent from this DTO, and `whitelist: true`
silently strips unknown body fields, so a client sending it got a 200 and no
change. Its only writer was the CSV pay-structure import — a technician on a
negotiated mileage rate could only be set up by uploading a file.

Independent of `splitType`: travel is reimbursed the same way whether the
member is PERCENTAGE, HOURLY or FLAT, so unlike the split fields this is not
cleared when the split type changes.

payrollDriveTimeRateCents.description:
Per-member drive-time rate, in cents per hour — `null` clears the override so
the member falls back to the org default. Same story as
`payrollMileageRateCents`: read at compute time, effective-dated, and until
now unreachable from any API.

payCurrency.description:
WHICH CURRENCY THIS PAYEE IS PAID IN — ISO-4217, or `null` to clear the
override so they fall back to the org's `defaultCurrency`.

Sits here beside the split and travel rates because it is a fact about the
same person's compensation, and beside `employmentType` on the screen for
the same reason: both describe how the org is engaged with them. An org that
pays Canadian technicians in CAD and outsourced editors in USD sets this on
the editors and leaves everybody else alone.

Three states, all meaningful and all distinct on the wire — the same shape
the travel-rate overrides above use, and the same reason: `whitelist: true`
strips an unknown key silently, so the client must send exactly one of
omitted / `null` / a value, and the service branches on `!== undefined`.

`@ValidateIf` lets an explicit `null` through: `@IsOptional()` alone would
accept it, but `@Length` would then also have to (it does not), so the
clear-the-override case needs the guard to be skipped rather than satisfied.

apiKey.description: The provider API key. Stored encrypted (AES-256-GCM); never returned by any read route.

label.description: Your own name for this key, shown on the settings screen.

secretKey.description: The Stripe secret key (sk_live_…, sk_test_…, or a restricted rk_… key). Stored encrypted (AES-256-GCM) and NEVER returned by any route, in any form. A restricted key scoped to payments is preferred over a full secret key.

publishableKey.description: The publishable key from the SAME Stripe account and the SAME mode. It is published to browsers and to the mobile SDK, so it is not a secret — but it is stored beside the secret key because the pair must not drift.

webhookSecret.description: The signing secret (whsec_…) of the webhook endpoint you created in your own Stripe dashboard pointing at the URL this route returns. Stored encrypted and never returned. Omit it on a key rotation to leave the existing one in place.

label.description: Your own name for this key, shown on the settings screen.

enabled.description: True to route this company's payments through its own Stripe account and key. False returns them to the platform account. Reversible at any time; the stored credentials are kept either way.

days.description: Trial length in whole days from now. Mutually exclusive with endsAt.

endsAt.description: Explicit trial end as an ISO-8601 timestamp. Mutually exclusive with days. Must be in the future and no more than 730 days out — the same ceiling `days` carries, enforced in OrgTrialsService.

note.description: Why this trial was granted — shown on the staff trials report.

phone.description:
REQUIRED — a customer added through this route is a customer being signed
up, and whoever books their shoot must be able to phone them.

SCOPE, deliberately narrow. This is `POST /customers` only: the four
staff-facing "Add customer" forms and the iOS invite sheet. It does NOT
touch the paths that legitimately have no phone to offer, all of which
stay permissive on purpose:

 - `UpdateCustomerDto` (PATCH /customers/:id) — an existing phone-less
   customer must stay editable for name, notes, brokerage and everything
   else. Demanding a phone in order to save an unrelated field would lock
   staff out of records they can edit today.
 - `POST /customers/import`, the bulk importer and the Aryeo migration —
   these call `CustomersService.findOrCreateCustomer` directly and never
   construct this DTO. A historical migration of thousands of contacts,
   many with no number on file, must not fail row by row.
 - Every auto-provision path (invite acceptance, JIT provisioning in
   JwtStrategy, loyalty streak rows, customer-portal lazy creation, demo
   seeding). Several of those run inside token validation and have no
   request body at all, so there is nowhere to put a phone; enforcing
   there would lock existing users out of the API entirely.

`OrganizationCustomer.phone` itself stays NULLABLE in the schema. A NOT
NULL column would fail outright against existing null rows, and
`prisma migrate deploy` runs in one transaction BEFORE the new image
serves, so it would also break the auto-provision paths above mid-deploy.
The requirement belongs at the request boundary, not on the column.

Tightening this in a single deploy is safe because `phone` was ALREADY a
declared field here — under `forbidNonWhitelisted` a brand-new field would
have 400'd the whole request whichever side shipped first.

additionalEmails.description: Secondary email addresses. The `email` above stays the primary/default.

additionalPhones.description: Secondary phone numbers. The `phone` above stays the primary/default.

row.description:
The row's line number IN THE OPERATOR'S FILE (header = 1), not its index in
this request. The client chunks a large file across several requests, so an
index would report "row 3" for row 1003 and send someone to the wrong line.

id.description:
The `id` column the export writes. It is the STRONGEST match this importer
has and the reason a round trip is exact: a directory row with no email and
no phone has no other stable identity, so without it re-importing an
unchanged export would mint a fresh copy of every such customer.

teamName.description:
The team this row's customer belongs to. Stored ONCE per team, on the
owner's `OrganizationCustomer.brokerageName` — the portal team identity the
owner sets themselves — never copied onto their rules.

teamOwnerEmail.description:
WHO THE TEAM BELONGS TO. A sharing team is owner-centric — it is literally
"this user plus everyone named on their standing rules" — so a team cannot
be created without naming its owner, and a row that names a team without a
resolvable owner is a bad row, never a silent skip.

teamRole.description: ADMINISTRATOR | AGENT | ASSISTANT, or OWNER on the owner's own row.

rows.description:
Capped at 1000 to match BulkDeleteCustomersDto's ceiling; the webapp chunks
a larger file into consecutive requests and aggregates the results, which
is safe because every step of the import is idempotent.

userId.description:
Either an existing account or an email address. An account joins
immediately; an unknown email is INVITED and joins on accept.

email.description:
Deliberately NOT `@IsEmail()`. The roster UI can save while someone is
mid-type, and a 400 on a half-typed address is worse than a row that
never resolves — the service lower-cases and looks it up, and an address
that matches nobody becomes an invitation rather than an error.

role.description:
OWNER is rejected by the service: ownership is transferred explicitly, not
handed out by adding a second one.

userId.description: The member who becomes OWNER. They must already be on the team.

teamId.description: Omit or send null to take the listing back out of its team.

contactPhone.description:
REQUIRED. This is the customer-facing public booking form — the single
biggest way an OrganizationCustomer comes into existence, and the one the
owner asked about: a provider was ending up with shoots booked by people
they had no way to phone.

Enforced on the DTO so it is a real requirement rather than a frontend
asterisk. Safe to tighten in one deploy because `contactPhone` was ALREADY
a declared field — under `forbidNonWhitelisted` a newly-added field would
400 the entire booking whichever side deployed first; tightening an
existing one only ever rejects a booking that was genuinely missing a
phone.

Retroactively safe: this validates the REQUEST, not the stored record.
`OrganizationCustomer.phone` stays nullable, so the thousands of existing
customers with no phone keep working everywhere. A returning customer who
books again simply fills the field in — and orders.service only ever
backfills a null phone, it never overwrites one.

promoCode.description:
A promotional offer's CODE, typed into the booking form's promo box.

DECLARED HERE OR THE WHOLE BOOKING 400s. The global pipe runs with
`forbidNonWhitelisted: true`, so an undeclared field is not silently
stripped — it is rejected, and the public page already sends this on every
submit where the box is non-empty. Omitting the declaration would take down
every public booking for every org, not merely the promotional ones.

Evaluated the same way `bookingFormId` is: a typed code is tried first and,
if it refuses, falls back to the link's own offer rather than costing the
customer the reduction they already had. See
`PromotionClaimService.previewForCart`.

orgId.description: Provider (COMPANY) org the booking is placed against.

customAddOnIds.description: Money Model v3 — Build-Your-Own picker selection (no packageId).

byoLayeredAddOnIds.description: Ordinary add-ons layered on top of a BYO cart (charged at list price).

addressLine1.description:
Street address of the property. Only used to GEOCODE when `lat`/`lng`
aren't supplied — the checkout paths (`createPublicOrder`,
`createCheckoutSession`) run the address through `resolveAddress` and price
the service area off the geocoded point, so a quote that skipped that step
priced against the base catalog while the charge priced against a service
area with overridden package/insurance prices. Send the same address fields
the order submit sends and the two agree.

Optional: omitting them (as the native iOS path does, which always has
coordinates) reproduces the previous behaviour exactly.

countryCode.description:
Property country (ISO-2). Send it whenever the booking captured one: it
stops a non-Canadian postcode being read as a Canadian FSA, so the quote
and the charge agree for foreign addresses too.

treatMissingTimeAsRequested.description:
When true, an order with no `scheduledTime` counts as REQUESTED scheduling
— the rule the public booking path applies. The authenticated agent path
uses `schedulingMode` verbatim, so it leaves this off.

applyLoyaltyCredits.description:
Loyalty credits the customer wants spent on this order — the SAME two
fields `CreateOrderDto` carries, so the quote can be asked the same
question the checkout will be asked.

They were missing here, and that was the original hole: the checkout paths
have always deducted credits from the Stripe amount
(`chargeableFromCheckoutTax(checkoutTax, creditsAppliedCents)`) while
`grossTotalCents` — documented as "exactly what the card will be charged" —
could not even see them. A customer with credits was quoted one number and
charged a smaller one. Smaller is not harmless: the confirm screen is the
only place the reduction is visible, so a credit balance silently
evaporated with nothing on screen saying it had been spent.

redeemEntitlementId.description:
LoyaltyEntitlement the customer intends to redeem on this order.

Quoting NEVER reserves and never spends — this route creates nothing. It
answers one question: if this reward were applied to this exact cart, what
would the card be charged, and if it could NOT be applied, why not. The
"why not" is the point: a `free_package` reward is 100% off the MATCHING
package's line, so a cart that does not contain that package cannot use it.
Returning it as inapplicable-with-a-reason is the whole contract —
silently pricing it at zero would show the customer a reward they still
hold as though they had just spent it.

Ownership is checked against the CALLER. `POST /orders/quote` is `@Public()`
so the anonymous booking portal can price a cart, and `JwtAuthGuard`
populates `req.user` best-effort there; with no caller the reward comes
back `requires_sign_in` rather than being priced. The unauthenticated
booking flow cannot redeem, by design.

bookingFormId.description:
The promotional booking link this cart is being priced through.

THE FIELD WHOSE ABSENCE WAS THE BUG. A booking form can carry an offer, and
the public page advertised it with "Included with this booking. It is
applied automatically, with nothing to enter" — while this endpoint, which
produces the only total the customer ever sees, was never told which form
they had arrived through. It could not price the offer even in principle,
so the review screen showed full list price under a banner promising the
opposite, and the invoice then charged that full price.

Quoting NEVER claims. The slot is taken at submission, so an abandoned cart
cannot burn a claim out of a capped campaign.

promoCode.description:
A coupon/offer code the customer typed on the review step.

Takes precedence over the link's own offer — one booking settles at most
one incentive — but a code that turns out to be invalid does NOT cost them
the link's offer. See `PromotionClaimService.previewForCart`.

contactEmail.description:
The address the customer has entered, when the flow has reached it.

Offers can be `newCustomersOnly`, and whether this person is already a
customer is not knowable on the client and must never be. The server
answers, and only about a person whose own address the caller supplied —
the same contract `GET /booking-forms/public/:id/promotion` already uses
for the banner. Without it an acquisition offer prices optimistically here
and is then refused at submission, quoting a total that is never charged.

phone.description:
REQUIRED. Creating a brand-new customer record inline on an order is a
signup — the provider ends up with a job to coordinate and needs a number
to call. Enforced here on the backend, not just with a frontend asterisk.

Safe to tighten in a single deploy: the field was ALREADY declared on this
DTO, so a frontend that ships before the backend keeps working (it was
always allowed to send `phone`), and a frontend that ships after is already
collecting it. Adding a NEW field would have 400'd the whole request under
`forbidNonWhitelisted` in one of the two orders — this does not.

Only bites when `newCustomer` is supplied at all; ordering for an EXISTING
customer sends `customerId` and never touches this object, so no existing
phone-less customer is blocked from having an order placed for them.

redeemEntitlementId.description:
LoyaltyEntitlement the customer is spending on THIS order — the reward
they were shown on the confirm screen. Single use: the checkout paths hold
it (`pending` → `reserved`) before the card is touched and fulfilment
burns it (`reserved` → `redeemed`), both as conditional UPDATEs guarded on
the current status.

It has to be a field on THIS class and not an inline `@Body()` literal:
`ValidationPipe` runs `forbidNonWhitelisted: true`, so an id sent against a
DTO that does not declare it is a 400 rather than a silently ignored
reward — and a route whose body has no DTO class at all is skipped by the
pipe entirely, which on a route that hands out free packages would be free
inventory.

The SERVER decides what it is worth. Nothing about the reduction is taken
from the client: `resolveRedeemableReward` re-reads the entitlement, checks
it belongs to this customer in this org, and prices it against the cart it
was actually applied to.

discountId.description:
An `OrgDiscount` the STAFF member booking this job is attaching to it —
by row id (a named markdown the org configured) or by coupon `code`.
Send exactly one; both, or a blank, is refused as `ambiguous_request`.

── WHAT THE CLIENT DOES NOT GET TO DECIDE ─────────────────────────────────
Neither field carries an AMOUNT, deliberately. The server re-reads the
`OrgDiscount` row in the PROVIDER's org, re-prices it against the invoice
it actually built, and clamps it — see `priceCoupon`. A client that could
name its own reduction would be a client that could make any order free.

── AND WHO GETS TO SEND THEM ──────────────────────────────────────────────
`POST /orders/create` is reachable by customers, so declaring these on the
DTO does NOT authorize them: `BookingIncentivesService.assertMayApplyIncentives`
checks `invoices.discount:write` IN THE PROVIDER ORG before either is
honoured. They are declared here because `ValidationPipe` runs
`forbidNonWhitelisted: true` — an undeclared field is a 400, which would
make a coordinator's coupon look like a broken booking.

── AND WHICH ROUTES CAN ACTUALLY SETTLE ONE ───────────────────────────────
ONLY the doors that raise an INVOICE: `POST /orders/create` on its
invoice-after-delivery branch, and the staff New Project door. A coupon is
a flat post-tax snapshot off a taxed invoice, and the card-at-checkout
routes (`POST /orders/checkout`, `POST /orders/native-checkout`, and
`POST /orders/create` when the provider org requires upfront payment)
charge before any invoice exists. Those routes REFUSE these two fields
with a 400 rather than ignoring them — see
`OrdersService.assertCheckoutCannotCarryCoupon`. `redeemEntitlementId`
above is different and IS honoured there, because a reward reduces the
cart's taxable base before the charge.

quality.description: Download quality tier. 'print' (default) zips original/print-quality files; 'web' zips the web/MLS-quality variant (mls → webReady → original fallback).

role.description: Role being rated: TECHNICIAN, EDITOR, PROJECT_MANAGER, or COMPANY

rateeId.description: User ID of the person being rated (null for COMPANY)

orgId.description: Organization ID (set when rating the company)

ratings.description: Array of ratings for team members and/or company

webDownloadUrl.description:
Signed, ready-to-use download link for the WEB / MLS quality variant
(2048px mls → 1920px webReady → original fallback). Forces an attachment
save. Null only when the media is not an image / has no original at all.

webReadyCdnUrl.description: Direct 1920px web-ready CDN URL (no redirect, no expiry), if generated.

embedUrl.description:
Absolute, zero-chrome embeddable player URL for the download-centre iframe
snippet (`/embed/video/:token/:mediaId`). VIDEO rows only; null for every
other media type and null when paywalled (an embed would stream the file
past the paywall). Points at the org's white-label host when one is
verified, else the platform frontend origin.

pendingDeliverables.description:
Ordered deliverable types the client purchased that have NOT been released
to them yet — the "— in production" chips on the download centre. Values are
MediaType strings, preserving the project's ordered sequence.

Derived on the RELEASE basis once the order has any `ProjectDeliveryRelease`
row (ordered types minus the union of every send's `mediaTypes`), which is
the same basis the partial-delivery email's "Still in production:" list uses
— the two are shown to the same person about the same order and must agree.

For an order with no release rows (everything delivered before partial
delivery existed) it falls back to the original derivation: ordered types
minus the media types actually present, with PROPERTY_WEBSITE and a
deliberately-unpublished VIRTUAL_TOUR excluded.

awaitingFinalDelivery.description:
True when the most recent send released only PART of the order, so the
client is looking at a delivery that is not finished.

Approval is what flips the project to DELIVERED and publishes the property
website, so it must not be offered here — `approveDelivery` refuses it, and
this flag is what stops the page rendering a button that 400s. Separate from
`canApprove` on purpose: the reader is still the approver and still gets
"Request changes", they simply cannot sign off yet.

viewerAuthenticated.description:
Whether THIS request carried a session the API accepted — i.e. whether the
flags above were computed for a signed-in person or for an anonymous
link-holder.

Exists because the two are indistinguishable from the client otherwise, and
they need opposite handling. `GET /delivery/:token` is `@Public()` with
optional auth: a stale or expired bearer token is silently ignored (no 401,
so nothing triggers the client's refresh) and the page renders an anonymous
payload while the app shell still shows the user signed in. Read as "the
customer is not recognised", which is what put "Only the customer can add
comments." in front of actual customers.

The client compares it against its own session: signed in locally + false
here = the credential didn't travel ⇒ refresh and refetch, don't tell the
reader they're the wrong person.

canViewDiscussion.description:
Whether the viewer may see the customer discussion at all. True only for
org team members and the linked customer — never an anonymous holder of the
public delivery link. Gates both the comments payload and the discussion UI.

deliveryChatCutoffAt.description:
When the shown discussion starts — the instant the project was FIRST
delivered. Messages before it (the pre-delivery scheduling/ops thread) are
filtered out SERVER-SIDE, so they never reach this public page. Null when no
delivery instant could be resolved (legacy/imported projects): the whole
thread is shown and the UI renders no cutoff marker. NOT interchangeable
with project.deliveryEnabledAt, which is the LATEST delivery and moves on
every re-delivery.

downloadEnabled.description: Whether bulk download is available (requires storage backend)

maxDownloadFiles.description:
Server cap on files per bulk ZIP (MAX_MEDIA_FILES_PER_ZIP). Lets the
 download dialog warn before a request that would 400 with TOO_MANY_FILES.

canRetryArtifact.description: Whether user can retry failed artifacts (OWNER/ADMIN/PROJECT_MANAGER only)

isStaffViewer.description:
True when the viewer is the SERVICE PROVIDER's side of this delivery, not
the client. Gates staff-perspective copy — a preview banner, an
"awaiting the customer" note — which otherwise renders to the customer and
talks about them in the third person on their own delivery page.

canDownloadUnpaid.description:
True only when the delivery IS paywalled (a blocking invoice is outstanding)
AND the viewer is staff of the organisation that owns the project — an
elevated OrganizationMember of `project.orgId`, per
`PaywallService.isOwningOrgStaff`.

Staff may pull unpaid deliverables; customers may not, and neither may the
linked agent-customer who is PERSONAL_OWNER of their own organisation. When
this is true the download centre keeps its download affordances on screen
and takes their URLs from the AUTHENTICATED `/delivery/:token/staff/*`
routes — every URL in `media` here still points at the public token routes,
which paywall unconditionally.

False for everyone on an unpaywalled delivery (nothing to be exempt from).

hasRated.description: Whether the customer has already rated this project

unbrandedListingUrl.description:
MLS-safe copy of `listingUrl` at its OWN address —
`/listing/<slug>/unbranded`, a distinct route rather than a flag on the
branded one, because the MLS data model holds two separate URLs
(`VirtualTourURLBranded` / `VirtualTourURLUnbranded`) and boards judge the
destination the link resolves to. It renders from a payload that never
carried the org, the agent or their contact details: no team or contact
section, no "Presented by" eyebrow, no footer, no provider name in the
title/OG/JSON-LD, and no company favicon. Safe to paste into an MLS
"Virtual Tour" field. Null whenever `listingUrl` is null.

artifactId.description: ID of the artifact to retry

code.description: Coupon code. Present => this is a coupon (uppercased on write, unique per org). Omit / null => a named discount preset.

value.description: PERCENT: whole percent 0..100. FIXED: amount in cents.

active.description: Whether the discount is active (default true)

offerKind.description: Makes this a claimable offer rather than an invoice discount. One of: free_items, discount_next_order_pct, discount_next_order_cents

maxClaims.description: Total claims allowed. Omit for unlimited.

code.description: Coupon code (uppercased on write, unique per org). Pass empty string / null to clear the code and make it a named discount.

value.description: PERCENT: whole percent 0..100. FIXED: amount in cents.

offerKind.description: Makes this a claimable offer rather than an invoice discount. One of: free_items, discount_next_order_pct, discount_next_order_cents

maxClaims.description: Total claims allowed. Omit for unlimited.

typeOther.description:
The agent's own words for an OTHER slot. 120 chars because every surface
that renders it (job feed card, detail panel, listing row, active-job card)
shows it on one line in place of a type label.

turnaroundHours.description:
Hours to deliver, from assignment. Overrides the job's default for this
one service — photos in 24h next to a floor plan in 3 days is the normal
case, not an edge case.

defaultTurnaroundHours.description:
The turnaround for the whole job, copied onto every slot that does not
override it. Optional: an agent with no strong view leaves it unset and
the work is simply unmeasured, which is honest. A required field on the
wizard's longest step gets a guess typed into it, and a wrong deadline is
worse than none.

targetedProviderIds.description:
Optional list of provider userIds to target with this job. When set,
only the listed providers (and the job's creator) can see and bid on
the job — public marketplace browsing skips it. An empty list means
the job is open to the whole marketplace.

body.description:
Trimmed before validation, so a body of spaces is caught as empty rather
than stored as a blank bubble.

amountCents.description:
The proposed price, in cents. Required and positive: a negotiation that
can reach zero by accident is one that can assign a slot nobody gets paid
for, and a $0 authorization fails downstream anyway.

message.description: Why. Optional — a number on its own is a valid counter.

serviceArea.description:
Where the provider will travel to, in their own words — "Calgary and
surrounding areas", "Greater Vancouver, will travel for full-day shoots".

SELF-DECLARED, and that is fine here in a way it is not for
`insuranceVerified`. This is a statement of preference the provider is
entitled to make about themselves; insurance is a claim that a human
reviewed a document, which a checkbox cannot satisfy. That is why one of
these ships and the other stays "Coming soon".

Free text rather than a picker because a provider's real coverage is a
sentence with conditions in it, and a dropdown of cities would force them
to pick the nearest lie.

filename.description: The pano file name, e.g. "<spotId>.jpg". Used as the deterministic key.

visitId.description:
The id returned by the surface's own view route (`/listings/:x/view` or
`/tours/:id/view`). One table serves both surfaces, so one endpoint
reports duration for both.

seconds.description:
Seconds on the page. Integer — the column is an Int, and a float would
throw at the database rather than at the edge.

ZERO IS VALID AND MEANINGFUL: it is a real bounce, and it is not the same
thing as never reporting (which leaves the column null). `@Min(0)`, not
`@Min(1)`, for exactly that reason.

fbc.description:
Meta's OWN cookies, read verbatim from `document.cookie`.

`_fbc` is the click cookie and `_fbp` the browser cookie. When the browser
can hand them over they beat anything we derive, because they are the exact
values Meta itself wrote; `fbc` in particular can only otherwise be
reconstructed as `fb.1.<click time>.<fbclid>`, and a reconstruction whose
timestamp is off by a session does not match.

pageUrl.description:
The page the form was submitted from, for Meta's `event_source_url`.

Sent by the client rather than reconstructed here because the property
website is served on the ORG'S OWN verified custom domain when it has one,
and only the browser knows which host the visitor actually used. A
mismatched source URL lowers the event's match quality.

trackingConsent.description:
`'denied'` when the visitor's stored tracking-consent choice says so.

`lib/tracking-consent.ts` is the browser's one predicate and it gates the
pixel injection, the `Lead` event and the attribution fields. It could not
gate the server-side send, because the server was never told — so flipping
that file's default to `denied`, which its own comments describe as the
single line a compliance decision changes, would have stopped every browser
tracker and left the Conversions API sending hashed buyer identities to Meta
regardless. Now it is told, and the attribution row records `DISABLED`.

visitorId.description:
Stable per-browser id kept in localStorage.

Optional by necessity — a browser that blocks storage, or a client build
older than this feature, will not send one, and those visits still count.
When it IS present it takes priority over the IP hash for deduplication,
because an IP hash collapses a whole office behind one NAT into a single
visitor.

utmTerm.description:
The rest of the UTM set: the keyword a search ad bid on (`utmTerm`) and
which creative was clicked (`utmContent`). They answer "which AD works", as
opposed to "which CAMPAIGN", which the three above already answer.

fbclid.description:
═══ CLICK IDS — captured at LANDING, because that is the only moment they
exist ═══

A UTM is for our report. A click id is the ONLY thing Meta, Google, TikTok
or Microsoft can match a later conversion back to a specific ad click with.
The click happens here, on the landing; the enquiry is submitted minutes or
days later, often after several page views. If this route does not store the
id, nothing downstream can invent it.

All optional, like everything else on this DTO: an organic visit has none,
and an old cached bundle that sends none must keep counting rather than
start 400ing.

fbp.description:
Meta's `_fbp` browser cookie, read verbatim from `document.cookie`. Paired
with `fbclid` it is what lifts a Conversions API event from "unmatched" to
"matched"; on its own it still identifies a returning browser to Meta.

mediaIds.description: Full grid order, 1-based positions assigned in this sequence.

captions.description:
mediaId → caption. Values are ENFORCED to be strings here — see
is-caption-map.validator.ts. A non-string value used to survive the pipe
and crash the public page's SSR.

hiddenMediaIds.description:
PHOTOS THE CURATOR HAS HIDDEN FROM THE PUBLIC SITE.

A per-website curation decision, NOT a delete: the media stays on the
project, in the delivery, and in every other deliverable. It simply is not
published on this property website — not inside a group, not in the
trailing "More photographs" gallery, not as the hero, and not as the
social-preview image.

It lives under `gallery` because photo curation already does (groups,
captions), but its SCOPE IS THE WHOLE SITE: `getListingBySlugOrToken`
removes these ids from the public payload before anything reads it, so
hiding still holds when the `gallery` section is excluded from
`includedSections`.

The list may never contain the hero — `ListingsService.enforceHeroNotHidden`
makes that a stored invariant on every save, so no consumer has to reason
about a hero that isn't allowed to render.

Bounded like every other array here: 1000 is far above any real delivery
(a shoot tops out in the low hundreds) and exists only to make the
pathological payload impossible.

photoOrder.description:
THE ORDER OF THE UNGROUPED PHOTOS, AS THE WEBSITE EDITOR ARRANGED THEM.

Ungrouped photos publish in the trailing "More photographs" gallery, and
until now their order came only from `Media.displayOrder` — which is set in
the job's Media tab, a staff-only surface. An AGENT editing their own
property website therefore had no way to order their photos at all: the
wizard's drag only worked inside a named group, and a site with no groups
had nothing draggable on it.

Deliberately NOT written through the media reorder endpoint. That endpoint
is gated on `canUploadMedia`, which opens with `project.orgId !== ctx.org.id`
— and an agent editing their own listing calls from their PERSONAL org, so
it refuses them. Reusing it would have meant widening media-write
permissions to make a cosmetic ordering feature work, which is the wrong
trade. This field is authorised by `resolveMarketingEditor` instead, the
same gate as every other thing on this page.

LEGACY — NO LONGER WRITTEN. The editor now arranges `Media.displayOrder`
itself (see `ListingsService.reorderListingPhotos`), so there is ONE photo
order across the website, the downloads centre and the delivery ZIP. Two
orders for one set of photos read as a bug to everyone who met them.

The field is still ACCEPTED and still applied when present, so a page
arranged before that change keeps the order it was published with instead
of reshuffling on deploy. The first drag on a listing clears it. Ids absent
from the list fall back to `displayOrder` behind the ones listed.

Bounded at 1000 like `hiddenMediaIds`, for the same reason.

photoUrl.description: Rendered in `` on the agency's branded domain — https only, and DISCARDED entirely when the editor is a customer (see ListingsService.stripCustomerOnlyForbiddenFields).

agentName.description: PER-LISTING OVERRIDES FOR THE AGENT CARD'S FOUR TEXT FIELDS. Blank means "use the profile" — see resolveListingAgent, which is the only thing that reads these. They exist so one listing can show a campaign or co-listing number without rewriting the agent's profile, which would change every listing they have ever had. DELIBERATELY NOT `@IsEmail` / a phone pattern. This route is a full-replace AUTOSAVE: the wizard PUTs the whole config as the user types, so a format rule here would 400 every keystroke of "k", "kk", "kkang@" and the editor would appear to stop saving until the address happened to parse. The values are rendered as text and as `mailto:` / `tel:` hrefs, where a malformed one is inert, so the cost of accepting it is a dead link the agent can see and fix — not a save they cannot complete. There is no `photoUrl` / `brokerageLogo` here on purpose: those are `` on the agency's own verified domain, which is exactly what stripCustomerOnlyForbiddenFields refuses to let a customer set on `team`.

includedSections.description:
`@ArrayUnique` because the renderer maps over this list directly: a
duplicated key rendered the same section TWICE, with a duplicate React key
AND a duplicate `id=` anchor — which breaks the in-page nav (both anchors
resolve to the first) as well as React reconciliation.

sectionContent.description:
`@IsDefined()` + `@IsObject()` are what make the nested tree above run at
all. `@ValidateNested()` alone SKIPS a property that is absent — so
`{"includedSections":["hero"]}` validated clean and stored `undefined`,
and `{"includedSections":[],"sectionContent":[]}` validated clean with an
ARRAY where every consumer (the public renderer, the OG-image builder, the
brochure path) reads `sectionContent.hero`. Two callers of the same route
could therefore be validated to two different contracts. `@IsObject()`
rejects the array form specifically; class-validator's `isObject` excludes
arrays.

The only writer is `sanitizeConfigForSave`
(apps/frontend/components/features/listing/wizard/wizard-utils.ts), which
always emits both keys and an object (`{}` when nothing is filled in), so
tightening this refuses nothing that was legitimately being sent.

templateId.description:
WHICH SITE TEMPLATE RENDERS THIS PROPERTY.

`@IsIn(SITE_TEMPLATE_IDS)` and not `@IsString()`, because this id selects a
RENDERER on a live public page: an unrecognised value does not degrade, it
leaves the page with nothing to draw, on a URL that is very likely already
printed on a brochure and attached to an MLS record. A 400 in the wizard is
infinitely preferable.

OPTIONAL, and absent means "leave it as it is" — NOT "reset to classic".
Every autosave sends the whole config, and a client build that predates
templates omits this key entirely; treating that omission as a reset would
silently pull every listing back to classic the moment one stale tab saved.
Clearing the choice is an explicit `null`.

NULL renders classic — the look every already-published property website has
today. Nothing is backfilled to a new template; see `site-templates.ts`.

metaPixelId.description:
═══ PER-LISTING AD PIXELS — the override of the company default ═══

The agent running ads on their own listing uses their own pixel; the company
sets a house default on `Organization.default*` and this overrides it, per
field. Same optional-means-leave-alone / null-means-clear rule as
`templateId`, for the same reason.

IDS ONLY, AND THAT IS A BOUNDARY. These are served to the PUBLIC property
website so the browser can load the tag — a pixel id is public by
construction, it ships inside the page's own script. The Conversions API
ACCESS TOKEN is a credential and is not settable here at all: it lives
encrypted on `OrgAdTrackingCredential`, reachable only through the
owner/admin-only `/ad-tracking` routes. A secret accepted on this route
would be published on the open internet by design, and it would be published
by the CUSTOMER, who can also edit this config.

── AND THE CHARACTER SET IS A BOUNDARY TOO ──────────────────────────────

`@Matches(PIXEL_ID_PATTERN)` and not a bare `@IsString()`. These ids are
interpolated into the BODY of an inline `<script>` on a public property
website (`fbq('init', …)` / `gtag('config', …)`), and THIS route is one a
CUSTOMER may call — so the value is attacker-influenced text on its way into
script source. `JSON.stringify` escapes it as a JS string, but a JS string
is not an HTML boundary: a `</script>` inside one ends the element for the
parser and everything after it is markup. The same rule is enforced again in
the service (`cleanPixelId`) because that is the choke point both writers —
this route and the org defaults — share; this decorator is what turns it
into a legible 400 in the wizard instead of a generic one.

`@MaxLength` stays: the pattern bounds length too, but the two are read by
different people for different reasons and the column is 120 either way.

`''` still clears — `@Matches` is skipped by `@IsOptional` for null, and the
empty string is caught by the service's blank check before the pattern.

accentPrimary.description:
═══ THE PAGE'S ACCENT PAIR — the agent's brand, not the agency's ═══

A property website is produced by the media company and handed to a SELLER
BY AN AGENT who belongs to a brokerage with its own colours. Until these
fields existed the page painted `Organization.brandColor` — the
PHOTOGRAPHY COMPANY's colour — and nothing could override it. These are
that override, per listing.

Same optional-means-leave-alone / null-means-clear rule as `templateId` and
the pixels above, for the same reason: every autosave sends the whole
config, and a client build that predates these fields omits them entirely.
Treating that omission as "clear" would let one stale tab silently repaint
a live client-facing page.

── `@Matches`, NOT `@IsString()`, AND THAT IS A SECURITY BOUNDARY ────────

These values are interpolated into CSS custom properties on a PUBLIC,
unauthenticated property website, and THIS route is one a CUSTOMER may
call — so the value is attacker-influenced text on its way into a
stylesheet. Today it lands in a React `style` object (set through CSSOM,
inert), but "the current consumer happens to be safe" is not a boundary:
the next consumer is a `<style>` block or an OG-image renderer, and there
`red;} body{display:none` is markup control rather than a colour. Hex or
nothing, refused at the write where there is a human to tell.

The same rule is enforced again in the service (`cleanAccentHex`) because
that is the choke point that also canonicalises `#ABC` → `#aabbcc`; this
decorator is what turns a bad value into a legible 400 in the wizard
instead of a generic one.

CLEARING IS AN EXPLICIT `null`, and only `null`. `@IsOptional` skips
validation for `null`/`undefined` but NOT for `''`, which therefore fails
`@Matches` and 400s — so the wizard sends `null` to go back to inheriting.
(The service's `cleanAccentHex` treats `''` as a clear as well, which is
what keeps a non-pipe internal caller from storing an empty string.)

externalId.description:
The pixel / measurement id this token authenticates FOR. Required, because
the credential is scoped to one pixel: that is what lets an agent's own
pixel on one listing have its own token alongside the company's.

accessToken.description:
Meta system-user access token. Long — Meta's are ~200 chars and can be
longer — so the bound is generous rather than tight; the real check is that
the platform accepts it before anything is stored.

hints.description:
Free-text bullets from the user — selling points, neighborhood
 facts, anything the fact sheet can't know.

showMinimap.description:
Render the floor-plan minimap in the PUBLISHED viewer. Defaults to true at
the column, so omitting this never turns an existing tour's minimap off.
The tour EDITOR always keeps its minimap regardless — this is not an
authoring setting.

startNodeId.description:
WHERE THE TOUR OPENS — the id of the TourNode a visitor lands on.

Distinct from a FLOOR's start node (`.../floors/:floorId/start-node`), which
governs floor switches. Without this the viewer opened on `floors[0]`, and
floors sort by level ascending, so every multi-floor tour opened in the
basement.

`null` CLEARS it (back to the lowest floor's start pano) — which is why the
validator has to allow null explicitly; omitting the key leaves it alone.
The service verifies a non-null id is a pano on THIS property before
storing it.

workflowId.description: Optional workflow override. Defaults to cinematic-long-video when omitted.

style.description:
DERIVED, for the same reason `WORKFLOW_IDS` above is. A hand-copied list
of looks would go stale the day a fifth is added and `whitelist: true`
would then reject it with a 400 that says nothing about why.

skyStyle.description: Evening sky for a day-to-dusk job.

blankTvScreens.description: Black out television screens showing a frozen frame or reflection.

lightFireplaces.description: Put a fire in the fireplaces.

greenLawn.description: Bring a tired or patchy lawn back to green.

removePhotographer.description: Take the photographer out of a mirror, wardrobe door or window reflection.

eveningLight.description: Relight the whole scene for evening. Not available — a request setting this is refused, and nothing is charged.

stagedRoomType.description: What a bare room should be furnished as. Virtual staging only — no engine is available for it yet, and a job requesting it is refused.

furnitureStyle.description: The furniture look for a staged room. Virtual staging only — not available yet.

removalScope.description: How much an emptying pass takes out. Furniture removal only — not available yet.

maskKey.description: Object removal only. The S3 key of a painted mask uploaded to this project. The service verifies the key stays within the caller's own project before it is used.

workflowId.description: Optional workflow override. Defaults to cinematic-long-video.

projectId.description: Vremly Project this AI job is anchored to. When supplied, outputs save back into the project's Media collection and the AI run appears in the project's history.

enhancement.description: Per-job enhancement choices. Only meaningful for enhancement workflows; ignored by the prompt-driven ones.

mediaIds.description:
The exposures, darkest-to-brightest as captured. Two is the smallest set
that is a bracket at all; nine is well past any real camera's sequence and
is here to stop a mis-built client sending a whole shoot as one group.

enhancement.description: Per-job enhancement choices, applied to the merged photo. Visible AI disclosure is deliberately absent — it is the org’s setting.

treatment.description: Which treatment to apply to this one photo. A treatment with no engine available is refused before any work is created.

options.description:
The choices the operator made in the panel, in OUR vocabulary.

Every field is optional and every field is validated. A client that sends
an option this treatment does not use is not an error — the provider reads
only what its capability honours, and the capabilities endpoint is what
stopped the screen offering it in the first place.

content.description: { text?: string, url?: string, caption?: string }

sectionTitle.description: Sidebar section grouping for classroom courses
Sidebar section grouping for classroom courses

bodyHtml.description:
Long-form rich-text body for the "Read more" dialog. Raw editor HTML —
the service sanitizes it to an allowlist before it is stored, so this
length cap bounds the pre-sanitize payload, not the trusted output.

name.description: Display name for the question set (e.g., "Social Media Questions"). Unique per org.

description.description: Optional internal description of when to use this set.

displayOrder.description: Display order in the admin list

applyToAllPackages.description: When true, this set is applied to every booking on this org regardless of selected package or add-ons.

applyToPackageIds.description: IDs of ServicePackage rows this set applies to.

applyToAddOnIds.description: IDs of PackageAddOn rows this set applies to.

requesterContactEmail.description: Email of the customer placing the request — used to verify ownership against the project customer record.

requestedTechnicianId.description: Specific technician the customer wants. Null = "anyone different".

status.description: Outcome — accept reassigns the project to the requested tech (or another picked tech); decline keeps current assignment.

assignTechnicianId.description: When accepting, optionally override the technician to assign (e.g., admin picks a different tech than the customer requested).

resolverNote.description: Optional note from the resolving admin to be relayed back to the customer.

appName.description: Display name for the iOS app — visible under the icon on the home screen + in Settings. Typically the company brand name. 2-30 chars.

brandColor.description: Hex primary brand color baked into the iOS build. Drives the app tint (buttons, accents, splash backdrop). Format "#RRGGBB".

splashColor.description: Hex splash background color. Usually #ffffff or an off-white tinted with the brand color. Optional — defaults to #ffffff.

brandLogoUrl.description: URL to the hosted brand logo (square PNG, transparent background recommended). Rendered on Splash, Auth header, and the in-app brand mark. The webapp form uploads the file to the same storage used for org logos and forwards the resulting URL here.

supportEmail.description: Support email shown in the app Settings.

privacyPolicyUrl.description: Privacy policy URL — required by Apple for App Store review.

requesterNotes.description: Free-form notes the company wants the Vremly team to know during review — special requirements, launch deadlines, etc.

keyId.description: App Store Connect API key ID (the JWT "kid").

issuerId.description: Issuer ID for the App Store Connect API key (a UUID).

privateKey.description: The downloaded .p8 private key contents (PKCS#8 EC key). Accepts the raw PEM or a base64 blob. Encrypted at rest; never returned.

status.description: Target status. Must follow the allowed transitions.

bundleId.description: Apple bundle ID for the new app. Must be unique across all whitelabel builds. Conventionally com.<companydomain>.portal. Required before the CI workflow can run.

ascAppId.description: App Store Connect app record ID (numeric).

reviewerNotes.description: Free-form notes from the reviewer (e.g. rejection reason, what is blocking the build, TestFlight invite instructions).

testflightUrl.description: TestFlight invite URL — stamped by the CI workflow once the build uploads successfully. Surfaced back to the requesting company.

appStoreUrl.description: App Store URL — set once Apple approves the app.

payrollMileageRateCents.description:
Travel rates accept an explicit `null` to mean "not configured".

`@IsOptional()` alone already skipped null, but nothing DECLARED that null
was a legitimate value, and the settings form omitted the key entirely when
a rate was cleared — so `updateConfig`'s skip-undefined loop left the old
number in place and the only reachable "off" value was `0`. A stored 0 then
reads as unconfigured downstream, which is why a deliberate zero and a
never-set rate became indistinguishable. Null is now the way to say "unset".

payrollTravelOrigin.description:
── `payrollHoursBasis` AND `payrollContractedOverrunToleranceMinutes` ARE
   NO LONGER SETTABLE ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

The basis chose which clock a shoot was paid on — the contract, the device
stopwatch (ACTUAL), or whichever was longer (GREATER_OF). Pay is the SHOOT's
own duration now, always, so a setting that claimed to change it would be a
control that changes nothing while reading as though it does. The tolerance
was GREATER_OF-only and has nothing left to gate.

`class-validator` runs with `whitelist: true`, so a client still sending
either key has it silently stripped rather than 400ing — which is the right
outcome here: an old browser tab must not be able to write a policy nothing
honours. The COLUMNS are untouched (all 902 production orgs read CONTRACTED
already) so historical runs keep their descriptions.

effectiveFrom.description:
The instant these rates became effective, ISO-8601.

A date-only value ('2026-06-01') is read as UTC midnight — pass a full
timestamp if the boundary matters in your local timezone. Must not be in
the future: this endpoint corrects history, it does not schedule.

payrollMileageRateCents.description:
Omit to inherit whatever was already in force at `effectiveFrom`; pass
 `null` to say "not configured" (which is NOT the same as zero).

payrollDriveTimeRateCents.description:
Same inherit/null semantics as `payrollMileageRateCents`. A deliberate 0
 means "we do not reimburse drive time" and is honoured silently; `null`
 means nobody has decided, and the line gets flagged instead.

reason.description:
Why the past is being corrected. REQUIRED on a backdated write (enforced in
the service, not here, because it depends on `effectiveFrom` vs now) — this
is money, and an audit row that says only "someone changed the June rate"
is not an audit trail.

periodStart.description: First day to pay. Normalised to local midnight in the ORG's timezone.

periodEnd.description:
LAST day to pay — inclusive, as an operator means it. Normalised to the
EXCLUSIVE start of the following local day, so 07-01 → 07-31 pays all of the
31st and 08-01 → 08-31 starts exactly where it stopped: no boundary instant
payable twice, and no 24-hour dead zone between periods.

allowOverlap.description:
Deliberate operator override to compute a window that overlaps an existing
run. Does NOT re-enable double payment — anything a finalized run has already
claimed still shows at zero — it only permits the overlap on purpose. Without
it an overlapping window is refused with a 409 naming the clashing runs.

payDate.description: Intended payment date. Required before generating a provider handoff.

periodEnd.description: Inclusive last day, same semantics as CreatePayrollRunDto.

reason.description:
WHY. Recorded on the `payroll.incentive_rule.backdated` audit entry for every
rule this writes, exactly as a hand-written backdated rule records one —
this awards a bonus on work that is already finished.

Optional at the API because the server always composes one naming the run
and its period when it is omitted. An operator's own sentence is better
evidence than a generated one and always wins; a generated one is better
evidence than a required box filled with a full stop.

amountCents.description:
MAY BE NEGATIVE (a deduction or clawback).

Not accepted on a `LINE_REMOVAL`, which derives its cents from the line it
removes: a removal whose amount was typed could half-remove a line, and a
line that is 90% removed is a number nobody can explain.

workKey.description: The unit of work this corrects. Omitted = the whole person's payout.

payrollItemId.description: Which payee's line this row lands on. Verified against the run.

workKey.description:
The unit of work being adjusted. REQUIRED here, unlike the single-line
route: a bulk request is by definition about specific lines, and a batch of
person-scoped lumps is the exact anti-pattern this feature replaces.

amountCents.description: MAY BE NEGATIVE. Not accepted on a `LINE_REMOVAL` — see the create DTO.

reason.description:
Per-row, so a batch can carry one reason per line where the lines differ.
 Falls back to the request's `reason` when omitted.

The reason every row inherits unless it states its own. One of the two must
be present for every row — the service refuses a row that would end up with
no reason, because a reason is the only thing that makes an adjustment
legible a month later.

lines.description:
BOUNDED. Every row is a row in one transaction, and an unbounded batch is a
long-held lock on a run's items plus a request that can time out halfway
through money. 500 is far above any real correction and far below anything
that endangers the transaction.

amountCents.description:
MAY BE NEGATIVE. Refused on a `LINE_REMOVAL`: its cents are the exact
negative of what the line was priced at, and a typed figure could leave a
line 90% removed.

confirmNotPaidFromExport.description:
Explicit acknowledgement that nobody has been paid from this run's export.

Required only when the run carries an export marker (`exportedAt` /
`exportTarget`). Un-finalizing releases every work claim, so if a bookkeeper
has already paid from the downloaded CSV the next run prices and pays the same
work again — and CSV is the channel money actually leaves by here. A separate,
deliberately-named field rather than a flag folded into the reason string, so
it cannot be sent by accident; it is recorded in the audit log as its own fact.

`whitelist: true` strips unknown body fields silently, so this name must match
the client exactly — a typo would look like "no override sent" and 400.

organizationMemberId.description:
The member whose pay line this attestation is for, when the caller knows it.

`payrollOnSiteSecondsOverride` lives on the SHOOT, not on a (member, shoot)
pair, so it prices every technician assigned to that shoot and cannot be
scoped per person without a schema change. What CAN be enforced is that the
named member is actually one of the shoot's technicians — attesting hours
against somebody who did not work it is always a mis-key, and it silently
changes what a different person is paid.

TODO(blocked-by-schema): a per-member visit attestation needs a
`(visitId, organizationMemberId)` override table mirroring
`PayrollWorkAttestation`. Until then this field authorises the write; it does
not scope it.

payrollOnSiteSecondsOverride.description:
Attested on-site seconds, or an explicit `null` to CLEAR a previous
attestation.

The service used to write `dto.payrollOnSiteSecondsOverride ?? undefined`,
and Prisma reads `undefined` as "leave this column alone" — so once an
override existed, no request could remove it. A mis-keyed 8-hour attestation
outranks the booked window on every future compute, permanently. `null` now
clears it, and the audit entry records the value it replaced.

onSiteSeconds.description:
Attested on-site seconds. Bounded by the same 12-hour plausibility ceiling
 the GPS band uses, so an attestation cannot assert something a measured
 session would have been rejected for — and by the SAME constant the
 visit-level route uses, which had no ceiling at all.

vendorMapping.description:
`{ [OrganizationMember.id]: quickbooksVendorId }` — CONTRACTORS ONLY.
Intuit accepts only a Vendor as a Bill payee, so this is the contractor
rail and an employee must never appear in it.

employeeMapping.description:
`{ [OrganizationMember.id]: quickbooksEmployeeId }` — EMPLOYEES ONLY.
The SAME key as `vendorMapping` (the MEMBERSHIP id, not the user id),
because `exportRun` looks both up as `map[item.organizationMemberId]`.

⚠ `class-validator` runs with `whitelist: true`, so a key this DTO does not
declare is silently STRIPPED — no 400, no error, just a mapping that never
saves. This field must stay declared for the employee rail to work at all.

accountMapping.description:
`{ wages, reimbursement, wagesPayable }`. The first two are expense
accounts; `wagesPayable` is a liability account, and it is validated
server-side against the live QuickBooks chart of accounts — Accounts
Payable is refused, because QuickBooks requires a vendor on every A/P line
and an employee is not a vendor.

returnsHere.description:
Does the technician also RETURN here at the end of the day?

MUST be declared: `class-validator` runs with `whitelist: true`, so an
undeclared field is stripped silently — the request would look like it
succeeded and the return leg would keep going to the profile home base,
which is a pay difference nobody would see until a run.

note.description: Why. Shown to the technician, so it is bounded rather than free-form.

organizationMemberId.description:
The `OrganizationMember.id` who is owed. Pay is owed to a MEMBERSHIP, not to
 a user account that may belong to several orgs.

title.description:
What the line says on the pay run. Also becomes the `reason` on the
`PayrollAdjustment` it is materialised as, so the same words appear on the
item, in the CSV and on the QuickBooks Bill line.

amountCents.description:
May be NEGATIVE — a deduction (equipment recovery, a clawback) is an ad-hoc
payable line too.

ZERO IS REJECTED. A zero line is a mis-key, not a decision: it would sit in
the outstanding pool, be collected by a run, and materialise as a CA$0.00
adjustment that means nothing to whoever reads it later.

projectId.description: Optional job this line is about.

incurredAt.description:
WHEN THIS BECAME PAYABLE. Decides which run's period collects it, and is the
date the Pay Run Items table shows. Defaults to now, so a line entered for
today needs no date; set it explicitly to book a line into the period the work
actually belongs to.

amountCents.description: Zero is rejected for the same reason as on create.

mediaType.description:
The EXISTING `MediaType` enum, MINUS the non-deliverable storage buckets.
Nothing here privileges FLOORPLAN or VIRTUAL_TOUR — any type that somebody
can actually COMPLETE may carry a rate.

DOCUMENT is refused rather than accepted-and-ignored. A rate is only ever
paid on a completion, and a document is filed rather than completed (see
`SLA_NON_DELIVERABLE_MEDIA_TYPES`), so accepting one would write a real
`OrgMediaRateVersion` row that reads back as configured pay and can never
produce a cent. `@IsIn` and not `@IsEnum`, because `whitelist: true` strips
unknown KEYS but does not narrow a valid enum VALUE.

amountCents.description:
Integer cents. `0` is ACCEPTED and means a DELIBERATE zero — "we do not
piece-rate this type" — which is honoured silently. It is NOT the same as
leaving the type unrated: an unrated type has no version row at all and
raises `RATE_NOT_CONFIGURED` on a completion instead of paying CA$0.00.
Never write 0 to mean "unset"; the two are not recoverable from each other.

currency.description:
ISO-4217. Defaults to the org's own currency. A rate in a currency the run
 does not pay in is REFUSED at compute time, never converted.

effectiveFrom.description:
When this rate takes effect. Omit for NOW (the ordinary forward change).

A PAST instant is a backdated correction and requires `reason`. A FUTURE
instant is refused — see the service.

reason.description:
Why the past is being corrected. REQUIRED on a backdated write (enforced in
the service, because it depends on `effectiveFrom` vs now). This is money.

kind.description:
Which predicate decides whether the bonus is earned. `SLA_BEAT` today.

Validated against the values this BUILD can actually evaluate, not against a
free string: a rule naming a predicate the running code does not implement
would sit in the table paying nothing, or — worse, if the check were absent
from the engine too — paying unconditionally.

mediaType.description:
Restrict to one media type, or omit for every type.

Same narrowing as `SetMediaRateDto`: an incentive is a bonus paid ON a
completion, so a non-deliverable storage bucket (DOCUMENT) can never be its
target and is refused rather than stored as a rule that never fires.

amountMode.description: FLAT — pay `amountCents`. PERCENT — pay `percentBps` of the piece rate.

amountCents.description:
Integer cents, for FLAT. Required for FLAT and rejected as zero — a bonus
 that pays nothing is a rule that does nothing.

percentBps.description:
Basis points of the piece rate, for PERCENT. 10000 = 100%.

An INTEGER and not a float percentage, so the bonus can never arrive as
`12.5000000001` and round differently on two computes of the same run.
Capped at 10000: a bonus larger than the work itself is a mis-key.

currency.description: ISO-4217 for a FLAT amount. Defaults to the org's own currency.

label.description:
What the pay run calls this line. Shown on the review screen beside the
 money, so a reviewer sees WHICH rule paid rather than a bare figure.

config.description:
Kind-specific parameters. `SLA_BEAT` needs none; declared so a future kind
 can carry its own without a migration or a DTO change.

effectiveFrom.description:
── WHEN THIS BONUS STARTS APPLYING. Omit for NOW. ─────────────────────────

A PAST instant BACKDATES the rule over work that is already finished, and
requires `reason`. It is the same shape `SetMediaRateDto.effectiveFrom`
already has, and it exists for the same reason: an org that decides in
September to pay an SLA bonus for August has two ways to do it, and only
one of them produces figures the engine can reproduce.

This route used to refuse it outright, on the argument that a bonus minted
with a past date "retroactively awards money on completions that have
already been reviewed". Both halves of that are still true and neither is
an argument for refusing:

 • A FINALIZED or EXPORTED run cannot be recomputed at all
   (`PayrollRunService.recompute` refuses before reading a candidate), so
   no money any run has committed to can move.
 • On a run that CAN recompute, the alternative was a hand-typed
   `PayrollManualItem` — a number nobody can re-derive, that no rate ladder
   explains and that a second reviewer cannot check. Backdating the rule
   reprices through the same `evaluateIncentive` the engine always uses.

What the refusal was actually protecting was the reader's ability to tell a
bonus that was in force from one filled in later. That is now carried on
every award (`IncentiveAward.provenance`, from `createdAt` vs
`effectiveFrom`) and on every line (`basis.provenance`), so the protection
survives without the prohibition — and an EMPLOYEE's line still refuses to
move for a backdated rule, whatever this field says.

A FUTURE instant is refused, exactly as it is for a rate.

reason.description:
Why a bonus is being applied to work that is already done. REQUIRED on a
backdated write (enforced in the service, because it depends on
`effectiveFrom` vs now). Recorded on the audit entry. This is money.

projectIds.description:
Project ids to resolve lanes for.

`ArrayMaxSize(200)` is THE COST CEILING and it is deliberately equal to the
project list's own maximum page size: this endpoint runs three id-bounded
queries, so its worst case is pinned to one page of the board rather than
to whatever a caller feels like sending.

Unknown ids, and ids the caller has no staff standing on, are simply ABSENT
from the response — never 403. A 403 on a mixed page would fail the whole
board because of one card, and a per-id 403 would be an enumeration oracle.

mediaType.description: The media type being marked complete. Must be one the project ordered.
Which media type of this project the person is on.

userId.description: User id of the assignee (an org member).

mediaType.description: Which media type to re-enable automatic routing for.

outcome.description: ON_TIME | LATE | EXCUSED, or null to clear. EXCUSED removes the stage from BOTH sides of every rate.

note.description: Why. Recorded on the row AND in the audit log — an override with no reason is unreviewable later. null clears it.
